question.knowledge_point: Calculating the Derivative of an Inverse Function Using a Table
question.worked_solution:
The formula for the derivative of the inverse is

$$
({g}^{-1})^{′}(x)=\frac{1}{{g}^{′}({g}^{-1}(x))}.
$$

Substituting $x=-2,$ we have

$$
({g}^{-1})^{′}(-2)=\frac{1}{{g}^{′}({g}^{-1}(-2))}.
$$

From the table, we obtain ${g}^{-1}(-2)=1$ and ${g}^{′}(1)=8.$ Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}({g}^{-1})^{′}(-2) & =\frac{1}{{g}^{′}({g}^{-1}(-2))} \\  & =\frac{1}{{g}^{′}(1)} \\  & =\frac{1}{8}.\end{aligned}
$$
